Over the next few years I put everything in to working towards my dream. I completed my Masters by Research with at the perfect time to apply for a job as a part-time lecturer and part-time PhD student . I had achieved my dream.

So I did my A Levels and went to to study dance and theatre. Less than a week in I met Martin Hargreaves, a recent PhD graduate who was teaching our seminars. From that moment I knew I wanted to be an academic.

But the most I had to learn was about the culture of overwork in academia, and how damaging that was for me as a person. I burnt myself out and struggled so severely with my mental health I had to withdraw from my PhD.

After 5 years I moved to . I had some amazing opportunities there, including achieving a long held dream of making a dance piece about Monty Python, performed by our professional company , in which I had a cameo as a very serious choreographer.

But then things changed. I got a phone call from my dad - she had taken a turn for the worse and didn't have long left. I immediately got in my care and managed to get to her side with 45 minutes to spare. I held her hand as she passed away.

This was a defining moment for me. I almost missed me there for one of the people I loved most in this world. I knew if I hadn't seen her before she died, and been with her for her passing, I'd never have forgiven myself. So I quit my job.

This was not the most sensible thing in the world. I have no real plan, other than to move back to Devon and start again. I knew I didn't want to be an academic anymore, but I didn't think I was qualified to do anything else.

Miraculously, something came up at the ideal place - . It involved some teaching, and supporting #PGRs and #ECRs. I thought I'd give it a shot. And a day after we said goodbye to my beloved Nan, I interviewed for and was offered my current job
